text: **The DB backup is taken through SQLite's online backup path, rolls on a configurable schedule into `.backup/`, and never fails silently** (D35). Four arms, and the first is the one a plausible implementation gets wrong. **(a) NEVER a file copy.** The store opens WAL (`store.rs:183`), so committed transactions live in `intent.db-wal` until checkpointed; `VACUUM INTO` or `sqlite3_backup_*` only, and `fs::copy`/`cp`/a directory tar are all defects. **(b) The snapshot is restorable and PROVEN so** -- a restored snapshot opens, passes schema validation, and returns the same entity counts as the source. **(c) Rolling retention per day/week/month with configurable counts, read from `intent/.config/config.json` via `intent config`, and DB snapshots occupy their own namespace under `.backup/` so they never collide with `intent upgrade`'s `backup-<TIMESTAMP>/` rollback artefacts** (`intent_upgrade:117-121`) -- two mechanisms in one directory with different retention rules, where deleting the wrong one is the loss this AC exists to prevent. **(d) A failed backup SURFACES, AND SO DOES ONE THAT NEVER RAN** (`IN-AG-NO-SILENT-001`): this is the backup of the durable SSOT, and the natural implementation -- best-effort, on a timer, in a daemon nobody watches -- is exactly the one that fails silently. **The second half was missing from this AC's first form and was found by ic asking for a read path: a schedule that never fires produces NO FAILURE TO REPORT, so "surface the failure" does not cover it and a user cannot distinguish a working schedule from one that silently never started.** Required therefore: **`doctor` reports backup STALENESS** -- the newest snapshot's age against the configured schedule -- which detects never-ran without needing anything to have failed. That is the two-sided test, the same construction as the clock guard's check C, which catches an inbox going backwards by comparing two stamps to each other and needs no clock at all. `intent backup --list` answers **what snapshots exist** and is deliberately NOT the health report: one place reports health, and it is `doctor`. **Two settings are ruled NOT configurable** (ic, endorsed): the snapshot directory is fixed, because a configurable path is precisely how a pruner gets aimed at `intent upgrade`'s rollback namespace and would make this AC's own collision reachable through _supported configuration_; and there is no key that silences backup failure, because a switch to turn the warning off manufactures the silent failure and gives it a supported name
